Quantity: Add to cart Add to wish list Add to wish list Buy now swap-horizontal Add to compare Description Reviews (0) Used Greer Amps Sucker Punch Distortion Pedal This is a used Greer Amps Sucker Punch distortion pedal, tested and confirmed to be in full working order, and it comes complete with the original box. Hand-designed by Nick Greer and built by Greer Amps in Athens, GA, the Sucker Punch is a high-gain distortion pedal built around a JFET preamp driving a 386D chip amp section — a combination that produces amp-like distortion in the spirit of early JCM-style Marshalls, with huge volume on tap and a wide-sweeping tone control that goes from thick and saturated to cutting and articulate. What the Sucker Punch Delivers Where a lot of high-gain pedals turn to mush at higher settings, the Sucker Punch keeps note definition intact. Chords stay separated, single-note lines cut through a mix, and the tone knob has enough range to dial in anything from classic rock crunch to thick, saturated modern gain. It responds to guitar volume and pick attack the way a cranked tube amp does, which makes it just as useful as a stand-alone gain sound as it is a pedal to stack in front of an already-dirty amp for extra push. sources.excerpt: Greer Amps Sucker Punch Distortion - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Sucker Punch Distortion Posted By Pedal of the Day on Tuesday, June 23, 2015 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> I review a LOT of overdrive pedals. A LOT. While the majority of them sound awesome, once in a while I will plug one in and it blows me away right from the get-go, one that I immediately say to myself, “You have to find room for this on one of your pedalboards NOW.” One of these pedals is the Sucker Punch Distortion from Greer Amps, so let’s check it out! As soon as you unleash this thing onto your favorite amp of choice (tube-preferred, IMO), you will see what I’m talking about as far as tone and balls-out rock and roll are concerned. I felt like I was in the studio watching Slash and the boys record ‘ Appetite For Destruction ‘, except the tones from that great record were coming out of the amp in my practice space! Control-wise, there’s nothing revolutionary about the Sucker Punch. Volume, Gain and Tone are about as basic as it gets for a dirt pedal, but don’t let that fool you into thinking this is a one-trick pony, even thought it is a workhorse (hehe). The SP uses a JFET preamp to drive a 386D chip amp section, creating tones similar to early JCM amplifiers, some of the most coveted of the Marshall line. This stompbox is like having a Marshall in a box, with a huge amount of volume, great open and soaring amp-like tones and the crunch and meat of amp sounds heard on countless album recordings throughout the last 50 years. With a ton of range, great sounds and a really flamboyant yellow enclosure, the Sucker Punch is the complete package, without overdoing it or trying to cram too many unnecessary options into a perfect drive box. It’s not really a big surprise, as Nick and everyone at Greer Amps keep churning out great pedal after great pedal. This one really rocked my world, however, so cheers to you all in Georgia, and keep making this excellent gear for us all to enjoy! Specs: Face melting tone! JFET gain stage driving chip amp section! JCM-amp type distortion! Huge amount of volume on tap! Wide tone sweep, for thick or cutting settings! True Bypass! Uses 9Volt battery or standard neg. center, 2.1mm power supply.
